title: Apply modularization budgets to the entire plugin
summary: The 200 to 400 line modularity rule applies to the whole Elementor Implementation Toolkit, not only the Filter Controller. Admin, CPT, REST, Elementor, Support, assets, scripts, and tests all need domain/subdomain/module boundaries before receiving more complex feature work.
rationale: A plugin-wide line-count scan showed the architecture risk is not isolated to filters. StyleControls.php has 1568 lines, FilterPresetAdmin.php has 1487 lines, eit-admin.css has 1290 lines, eit-editor.js has 1025 lines, eit-frontend.js has 845 lines, ContentControls.php has 679 lines, CptManager.php has 650 lines, CptManagerAdmin.php has 622 lines, and FilterResolver.php has 606 lines. If the modularity rule only applies to filters, the same AI failure mode will reappear in admin UI, CPT management, REST save paths, support utilities, and assets.

decision.hard_rule: No authored plugin surface is exempt from line-budget review just because it is not a filter file.

line_budget.target_range: 200 to 400 lines is acceptable for normal authored plugin files.
line_budget.orchestrator_files: Prefer under 200 lines; hard review at 250 lines.
line_budget.module_files: Prefer under 320 lines; split or justify before 400 lines; block new feature work above 450 lines.
line_budget.oversized_debt: Above 800 lines is active architecture debt. Above 1200 lines blocks additional complex UI/control work in that area.

domain_scope: Elementor widgets, controls, dynamic tags, and renderers
decision.workflow_rule: Before adding non-trivial feature work to any plugin area, check whether the destination file is over budget. If it is, create or execute a modularization task first.

alternatives_considered: Apply the rule only to Filter Controller files
Allow admin and asset files to grow until they visibly break
Rewrite the whole plugin before any further feature work
Use line counts only as warnings without blocking new work
evidence: find/wc scan of wordpress/wp-content/plugins/elementor-implementation-toolkit reported multiple authored files above 600 lines.
FilterPresetAdmin.php and eit-admin.css are already above 1200 lines.
The current bug pattern came from patches entering oversized files with too many unrelated responsibilities.
risks: A global rule can feel slower because it blocks seemingly small feature work in oversized areas.
Line count alone is not architecture, so every split still needs behavior-preserving scope and verification.
Over-splitting without domain names can make navigation harder; split by real responsibility, not arbitrary size.
